title: Microsoft Edge: opt-in for launching Edge when Windows starts on managed devices
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, opt-in behaviour, policy controls and release-note dates are supported. Add the Windows policy configuration reference to support the explanation that mandatory policies prevent users from overriding them.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an opt-in experience for users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches when Windows starts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge will introduce an opt-in experience that allows users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts.

claims.claim: The roadmap names LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled for administrator management with opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
claims.quote: Administrators can also manage this behavior through the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy with opt-in, opt-out, and user-choice configurations.

claims.claim: Enabling the policy makes Edge launch visibly automatically when Windows starts.

claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, Edge does not launch automatically at Windows startup by default.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default.

claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn automatic launch on.

claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, users can enable or disable automatic launch at any time from settings.

claims.claim: Automatic visible launch is user-opt-in when no administrator configures the policy.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default. Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.claim: A mandatory policy value is enforced rather than being a default that users can override.
claims.quote: Mandatory policies override user preferences and prevent the user from changing the policy settings. Recommended policies provide a default setting that the user can override.

claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled licensing price meter"; Edge for Business licensing requirements and additional cost. Read the policy reference, roadmap, Edge for Business and Edge management service; no autolaunch meter was documented.

claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled licensing price meter" and Edge for Business licensing and additional cost. Read the policy reference, roadmap record and Edge for Business page; no autolaunch price was stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and policy reference describe a launch setting rather than documenting new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled with Edge autolaunch opt-in, banner frequency and management service. Read the complete roadmap description and policy reference: they describe visible launch, user choice and configuration, without new data access.

claims.claim: For an unconfigured policy, the policy page describes only the opt-in banner and user settings as ways to choose automatic launch.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner frequency admin center policy". Read the full policy reference; the unconfigured-policy paragraph describes the banner and user settings, without another decision mechanism.

claims.claim: The policy reference documents no separate admin-centre switch for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner frequency admin center policy"; Edge management service configuration. Read both references; the policy page itself lists Group Policy and registry settings, not a separate admin-centre switch.

claims.claim: The policy page says the banner appears periodically without giving a frequency.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner frequency admin center policy". Read the full policy reference and the Stable feature entries; the policy says "periodically shown an opt-in banner" without a numerical frequency.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The checked rollout sources give no fixed date for an individual tenant or for completion of the controlled rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled with Edge autolaunch opt-in and management service. Read the roadmap and Stable entries for versions 156 and 158; these give a month target and controlled-rollout notice, not tenant-specific or completion dates.

claims.claim: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled is the documented control for this particular opt-in experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner frequency admin center policy" and Edge management service configuration. Read the policy reference and Stable feature entries; they identify this policy, not another feature-specific control.
